finding: An IR edge whose source or target is a node that has children never reaches the canvas. React Flow refuses to create it and logs error #008; the connection is silently absent from the rendered diagram.
evidenceVerbatim: [React Flow]: Couldn't create edge for target handle id: "target-1", edge id: conn-... Help: https://reactflow.dev/error#008
how: console.warn was wrapped in the running app tab to capture React Flow's own warning, and `.react-flow__edge-path` counted in the DOM after Aceitar. Independently, each captured IR was re-analysed offline: an edge counts as container-touching when its source or target id appears as some other node's parentId.
correlation: domEdgePaths == irEdges - edgesTouchingContainer in all six runs, exactly. B-run1: 27 - 16 = 11 rendered paths, and 11 is what the DOM has.
notVirtualisation: `onlyRenderVisibleElements` appears nowhere in the codebase (grep), so the missing paths are not React Flow culling offscreen edges.
whyOnlyOneRun: Whether the failure fires depends on what the model wrote, not on the pipeline. Case A's model output happens to wire only leaf-to-leaf. Case B hit it once, in the run where the model wired 'ALB -> ECS service' and similar container-addressed edges, which is idiomatic AWS. It is latent in the other five runs, not absent.
scope: Reported, not fixed. Per the slice's mandatory stop, a new failure mode is the result of this slice; correcting it belongs to another slice with its own product decision.
